status: CLD MINIMIZER REFINED: BETA-EQUILIBRIUM EXACT, CRUST-CORE TRANSITION FOUND, NATIVE READER STILL PASSES
summary: The CLD minimizer was substantially improved. Three key upgrades: (1) cluster-phase beta-equilibrium root-find (bisection) now solves rho_Ip from mu_n(I) - mu_p(I) = mu_e exactly, with the gas treated as pure neutron (low-density inner-crust approximation); beta-equilibrium residual is now 0.000 at all densities (was 30 MeV before). (2) Nelder-Mead simplex refinement (no scipy dependency) starting from the coarse-grid best, in 3 free variables (f, log R_d, rho_I); the f=0.01 grid-sticking problem is resolved (f now ranges 0.004-0.667 smoothly). (3) eos.thermo now carries real mu_n/mu_p (per-baryon, rest mass subtracted) from the CLD cell, not the zero placeholder.

what_was_fixed.beta_equilibrium: Replaced the gas-phase beta-equilibrium (which had no sign change because mu_n - mu_p < mu_e at all rho_IIp in the gas, since the cluster grabbed all the protons) with a CLUSTER-phase beta-equilibrium: solve rho_Ip from mu_n(I) - mu_p(I) = mu_e where mu_e = electron_chemical_potential(f*rho_Ip + (1-f)*rho_IIp) with rho_IIp = 0 (pure neutron gas). This is the standard low-density inner-crust approximation. Bisection in [0, rho_I] finds the root in 60 iterations; residual is 0.000 at all tested densities (was 30 MeV with the old gas-phase formulation).
what_was_fixed.minimizer: Replaced the pure 5-variable coarse grid (f, R_d, rho_I, yI, rho_IIp = 5*7*4*5*4 = 2800 evaluations, no refinement) with a 3-variable coarse grid + Nelder-Mead refinement. The 3 free variables are (f, log R_d, rho_I); rho_Ip is solved from beta-equil (not free). Nelder-Mead: 120 iterations max, simplex in 3D, standard alpha=1/gamma=2/rho=0.5/sigma=0.5 coefficients. Total cost: ~175 coarse evaluations + ~120 simplex = ~300 per density point; runtime ~0.3-0.8 s per point (was ~2 s with the larger grid).
what_was_fixed.f_grid_sticking_resolved: Previously f stuck at 0.01 (the smallest grid value) for most densities because the coarse grid was too coarse and the minimum was at the boundary. Now f ranges smoothly from 0.004 (low density) to 0.667 (near transition), with R_d from 2.9 to 5.5 fm, matching the physical picture of small clusters growing as the crust-core transition is approached.
what_was_fixed.eos_thermo_mu: eos.thermo now writes mu_n_per = r.mu_n - M_N and mu_p_per = r.mu_p - M_P (per-baryon, rest mass subtracted, matching the FSU2 column convention where mu_n ~ -9.69e-3 MeV). Previously both were 0.

physical_results.R_d_range: 2.9 to 5.5 fm (nuclear-scale droplets; 40 fm at 0.075 is a boundary artifact)
physical_results.rho_I_range: 0.079 to 0.140 fm^-3 (near saturation, decreasing slightly as f grows)

GPPVA_DD2_refined_reconstruction.crust_core_transition: rho_B ~ 0.070 fm^-3 (CLD energy becomes HIGHER than homogeneous beta-equil matter). This matches the known DD2 inner-crust/crust-core transition density (~0.07-0.08 fm^-3).
GPPVA_DD2_refined_reconstruction.native_reader_test: PASSED - compose_eos.read_compose() returns EOSData with F shape (20,), Aav shape (20,) head [14.5, 15.1, 14.7], Iphase, Q1 (rho_B grid), Q2 parsed correctly.

CLD_vs_homogeneous_at_transition.rho_0.001: CLD -0.541 vs hom 0.933 -> CLD lower by 1.47 MeV (cluster favored)
CLD_vs_homogeneous_at_transition.rho_0.05: CLD 6.077 vs hom 6.125 -> CLD lower by 0.05 MeV (cluster still favored)
CLD_vs_homogeneous_at_transition.rho_0.07: CLD 7.661 vs hom 7.527 -> CLD HIGHER by 0.13 MeV (cluster dissolves)
CLD_vs_homogeneous_at_transition.rho_0.08: CLD 8.401 vs hom 8.340 -> CLD higher by 0.06 MeV (homogeneous stable)

remaining_issues.f_jump_at_transition: At rho_B = 0.075 the minimizer returns f=0.667, R_d=40 fm (grid upper bound) rather than f->1 (homogeneous). This is a boundary artifact of the R_d grid cap at 40 fm and the f cap at 0.95. The transition DENSITY is still correctly identified at 0.070; the post-transition cluster properties are not physical but the E/A is still correct (matches homogeneous).
remaining_issues.pure_neutron_gas_approximation: rho_IIp is fixed at 0 (pure neutron gas). At higher inner-crust densities this becomes less accurate; a full two-phase beta-equilibrium (mu_n(I) = mu_n(II), mu_p(I) = mu_p(II)) would refine rho_IIp > 0. The current approximation is the standard low-density limit and is adequate for the reconstruction demonstration.
remaining_issues.SPG_M1_deep_binding: Still unresolved (E/A = -45.76 vs target -16.14); needs separate investigation of the Gögelein Table I rho_sat or convention.
remaining_issues.DD-ME2/TW99/FSU2: Only GPPVA_DD2 reconstructed; the other 6 models need exact coupling-table extraction from their PDFs.
